smell_validity.evidence: A complete export feature is retained with no role under any supported configuration: every activation path sits behind compile-time-off constants (two bool gates and a zero depth ceiling), unreachable yet cross-referenced so unused-item lints stay silent. It tells one coherent shelved-feature story with a clean boundary from a config-gated rollout. Slight contrivance (parity sink selection, 'legacy-' prefix) keeps it short of reference quality.

maintenance_impact.evidence: Dead members are interleaved with near-identical live code across five pipeline modules, and guarded fragments occupy hot live functions (run, grid rendering, icon lookup). Tooling will never flag them, so future work on sorting, icons, metadata and rendering must repeatedly separate dead from live; removal restores clear module ownership rather than just shortening files.

development_plausibility.evidence: A rollout-gated then shelved machine-readable export fits lsd's pipeline naturally: comparators land beside live sorters, row formatting beside grid code, labels on Meta, in matching style with maintainer-voiced doc comments and plausible integration conventions. The deliberate dual guard grammars and row-parity sink choice show mild task shaping that ordinary evolution would not.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: The prompt turns a vague cleanup into a reliable contract: it gives the decisive tell (branches under permanently-off switches), the transitive only-called-by-export-members rule, a post-sweep for stragglers across the named pipeline areas, a warning that live look-alike members must be kept, and bounds the change to pure deletion with rendering, icons, orderings, CLI flags and config unchanged. This materially blocks enabling-instead-of-deleting, partial cleanup and unrelated redesign while leaving implementation order free.

semantic_diversity.evidence: Four distinct reasoning kinds: bool-const gate identification, recognizing the zero-ceiling unsigned comparison as never true (different grammar), dyn-dispatch reachability through the parity-selected sink, and whole-item removal of sole-caller chains versus surgical excision inside three live functions. Additionally the sort and metadata accessor pairs follow the same delete-with-caller rule, preventing a clean 5.

localization_burden.evidence: Scope spans five modules and cross-component combination is required: core's dead summary drives display's sink family, which drives Meta's accessors, and the sink trait's two implementations are only reachable through the boxed parity constructor, never by name at call sites. Textually adjacent live comparators and the live icon fallback must be identified as exclusions.

repair_coordination.evidence: Two locations share one rule: the sink family is referenced from both the core summary builder and the render hook, and the glyph chain from both the icon gate and the summary. Removing only one gate leaves references intact so the members cannot be deleted without compile errors across modules, but the compiler itself surfaces those mismatches rather than allowing silent divergence.

mechanical_resistance.evidence: One uniform rule — excise bool-const-false branches, then let the dead-code lint enumerate newly unreferenced members — repairs roughly half the locations (core gate, summary, sort pair, icon glyph chain, all const-off style). The hook guarding the sink family, formatter and Meta labels uses a zero-ceiling unsigned comparison instead, so a single pattern covers about 40–59 percent.

behavioral_risk.evidence: Multiple concrete wrong edits compile and pass all existing behavior unchanged: skipping the display-door cluster or the icon chain leaves self-referencing members behind warning-free, since the remaining branches are syntactically live and no tests were added for export members. Only reference-breaking over-deletions fail loudly; completeness failures are not checked by any test or diagnostic.

recommendation_reason: Deterministic validation passed and every Quality dimension meets the retention threshold.
